memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Whenever Aaron enters the Holy Place, he will bear the names of the sons of Israel over his heart on the breastpiece of decision as a continuing memorial before the Lord. Also put the Urim and the Thummim in the breastpiece, so they may be over Aaron's heart whenever he enters the presence of the Lord. Thus Aaron will always bear the means of making decisions for the Israelites over his heart before the Lord." - Exodus 28:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here God states the purpose of the whole breastpiece. Aaron bore the names of Israel over his heart whenever he entered God's presence. On his shoulders he carried their weight; over his heart he carried their names. Strength and affection together — the people were both borne and loved.

The phrase "over his heart" is repeated three times in these two verses. God wanted it unmistakable. This was not administration; it was love. The priest did not merely process the people's business before God. He held them close to his affections as he stood in the holy place.

This is our Lord Jesus exactly. He does not represent us reluctantly or mechanically. He carries us over His heart. The names engraved on Aaron's stones were written in gems; ours are written on the palms of God's hands (Isa 49:16). When Jesus stands before the Father for you, He is not fulfilling a duty. He loves you. Let that settle deep today: you are carried, and you are carried with affection.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I believe Christ intercedes for me with genuine love, not mere duty?
Do I carry others in my prayers with real affection, or only obligation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You carry my name over Your heart before the Father, and You do it in love. Thank You for such affection. Teach me to carry others with that same love. Amen.
